Lemma
[Splitting Lemma] \group Singular Homology

For $0\to A\xrightarrow {i}B\xrightarrow {j}C\to 0$, the following are equivalent: there is $p:B\to A$ with $pi=\mathbb {1}$; there is $s:C\to B$ with $js=\mathbb {1}$; and $B\cong A\oplus C$ compatibly with the sequence.
Proof

\sketch A retraction gives $b\mapsto (p(b),j(b))$; a section gives $(a,c)\mapsto i(a)+s(c)$. These maps are inverse isomorphisms, and the converse maps are projections and inclusions.

□
